transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. Refrigerant systems are sealed under high pressure; attempting to open them or add gas without specialist recovery equipment is illegal in the UK, dangerous for you (risk of frostbite or asphyxiation), and will permanently damage the appliance. Only a qualified engineer with proper certification can handle refrigerants. The fact that your compressor is running and the back of the fridge is warm suggests it is trying to cool, but not removing heat effectively from inside. This is most commonly caused by either a blocked airflow (often due to ice build-up in the freezer) or a failed fan that circulates cold air from the freezer to the fridge. To help narrow this down: Is there a thick layer of ice or frost building up on the back wall inside the freezer compartment?
no frost anywhere, the freezer back wall isnt even cold. its about 0C in there and everything has thawed. there is a fan going when the door is shut tho

Your mate was right to suspect 'regassing', but as I mentioned, you cannot do this yourself: it requires specialist recovery equipment and certification because R600a (the gas in your Indesit) is flammable. Please stop using the appliance if possible to avoid burning out the compressor further, and call a qualified refrigeration engineer. They will need to check for leaks and test the compressor's health before deciding whether it can be repaired or needs replacing.
